plan.concept: A homography maps a 2D plane to another, warping lengths, angles, and parallelism while keeping straight lines straight.
learningObjectives: Identify which geometric properties (collinearity) are preserved under a homography and which (angles, lengths, parallelism) are lost
Explain how perspective projection causes parallel lines to converge at vanishing points
Describe how camera tilt and rotation relative to a plane generate different homographic warps
plan.keyInsight: Even as parallel lines converge and angles distort under a homography, straight lines are guaranteed to remain perfectly straight.

interactions.label: Horizontal Tilt (Yaw)
interactions.effect: Compresses one side of the grid vertically while stretching the other, simulating a camera rotating horizontally.
interactions.teaches: How rotating a viewpoint creates perspective scaling where objects further away look smaller.

interactions.label: Vertical Tilt (Pitch)
interactions.effect: Compresses the top or bottom of the grid horizontally, simulating looking up or down at a surface.
interactions.teaches: How tilt alters the convergence of vertical parallel lines.

interactions.label: Show Vanishing Lines
interactions.effect: Draws dashed helper lines extending from the grid boundaries to show where they intersect in space.
interactions.teaches: That parallel lines in a scene always project to lines meeting at a shared vanishing point.

demo_steps.title: The Reference Grid
demo_steps.narration: Look at the flat, regular grid on the left. In this original state, all grid lines are perfectly parallel, intersect at 90-degree angles, and define equal-sized squares.
demo_steps.focus: The perfectly symmetrical, orthogonal structure of the reference grid.

demo_steps.title: Introducing Perspective Tilt
demo_steps.narration: Now, observe how the grid on the right deforms as we tilt it horizontally. Notice how the vertical lines on the right side shrink closer together and the horizontal lines begin to tilt and converge, mimicking perspective depth.
demo_steps.focus: The tapering of grid cells and the loss of parallel horizontal lines.

demo_steps.title: Preservation of Collinearity
demo_steps.narration: Let's apply both horizontal and vertical tilt. Even though the squares are now highly distorted quadrilaterals and angles are no longer 90 degrees, trace any line from end to end: it remains perfectly straight. This is collinearity preservation.
demo_steps.focus: The individual grid lines, showing they have no curves or bends.

demo_steps.title: Finding the Vanishing Points
demo_steps.narration: Turn on the vanishing lines. By extending the converging parallel lines beyond the grid, you can see them intersect at precise points in space. Under a homography, parallel lines always meet at these vanishing points.
demo_steps.focus: The intersection points of the extended dashed lines.

plan.reconstructionNotes: A side-by-side layout: Left panel shows a static, flat, black-and-white 4x4 square grid as reference. Right panel shows a dynamically warped grid based on interactive values. Use colored lines (e.g., orange for horizontal lines, blue for vertical lines) in both grids to help the user trace matching lines. When 'showVanishingPoints' is true, draw thin dashed lines of matching colors extending outward from the grid boundaries to their intersection points off-screen.
